verbalization: Doxorubicin is associated with Acute Myeloid Leukemia (AML) through a series of indirect pathways, with the disease being linked to the translocation T(9;11)(p22;q23), which is a known driver of AML. This translocation is also associated with the presence of the Inv3(p21;q26.2) or T(3;3)(p21;q26.2) chromosomal abnormalities. Doxorubicin's indication for AML includes the T(9;11)(p22;q23) variant, and it is also linked to the Inv3(p21;q26.2) variant through the drug's interaction with Glasdegib and Idarubicin, which are indicated for the same AML subtypes. The evidence suggests that Doxorubicin may be used in the treatment of AML with these genetic alterations, though the exact mechanism of action remains unclear. The scores from the paths indicate a moderate level of support for this relationship, but the evidence is not definitive, and further research is needed to confirm the therapeutic relevance of Doxorubicin in this specific AML subset.
